title: Comint timeout outcome_unknown without retry

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: Timing out while waiting for process output means the submitted command's outcome is unknown, not that it did not run.
hypothesis: A slow non-idempotent command submitted once through Comint should be classified `outcome_unknown' at the short deadline and later prove a single side effect.
minimal_fixture: One long-lived shell, one counter file, one submitted slow command, and two waits: short timeout then final completion.
predicted_behavior: The short wait should not see completion; the later wait should show the counter incremented exactly once.
observed_behavior:
early-done=nil outcome=outcome_unknown final-done=210 counter="1" output="sleep 0.6; n=$(cat /project/tmp/soma-comint-timeout-UsFT35/counter); n=$((n+1)); printf '%s\\n' \"$n\" > /project/tmp/soma-comint-timeout-UsFT35/counter; printf 'SOMA_TIMEOUT_DONE:%s\\n' \"$n\"
$ SOMA_TIMEOUT_DONE:1
$ "

independent_checks.name: short wait reached outcome_unknown before completion
submitted command eventually completed
independent_checks.detail:
sleep 0.6; n=$(cat /project/tmp/soma-comint-timeout-UsFT35/counter); n=$((n+1)); printf '%s\n' "$n" > /project/tmp/soma-comint-timeout-UsFT35/counter; printf 'SOMA_TIMEOUT_DONE:%s\n' "$n"
$ SOMA_TIMEOUT_DONE:1
$

independent_checks.name: non-idempotent side effect occurred exactly once
independent_checks.detail:
counter="1" output="sleep 0.6; n=$(cat /project/tmp/soma-comint-timeout-UsFT35/counter); n=$((n+1)); printf '%s\\n' \"$n\" > /project/tmp/soma-comint-timeout-UsFT35/counter; printf 'SOMA_TIMEOUT_DONE:%s\\n' \"$n\"
$ SOMA_TIMEOUT_DONE:1
$ "

counterexample: A retry after a timeout can duplicate non-idempotent work while still showing the expected final output.
derived_gym_requirement: Comint and process actions must represent timeout as `outcome_unknown' and block blind retry unless the operation is proven idempotent or externally canceled.
